# Review, pass 1 — odyssey-086 (Odyssey 17.409–507)

Reviewer: pass 1. Files read: runbook (Reviewer paragraph), conventions.md (rules, notes rules, house-table rows for the words of this part, rows for Books 14 and 17 especially), packet.md, units.json, new-renderings.md, odyssey-001/units.json (shape), odyssey-085/units.json (last units), the published odyssey-004/008/021/031/033/068/085 units for repeated lines. No modern translation consulted. `t` untouched; `ln`, `p`, `mark`, `v` untouched (checked by script: `t` of all 64 units rejoins to the packet exactly, every `ln` is the line the unit starts on, `p` falls exactly on Murray's paragraph starts, `l` has as many line breaks as `t`).

Totals: 20 changes in 13 units (0 high, 9 medium, 11 low); 0 scansion flags to scan (the packet lists none); one finding about a neighbouring part's file that this review may not edit (see the end).

Severity: high = wrong Greek-to-English or a note claiming something false that misleads the reader and affects meaning; medium = a note label or claim false of this form/line, or a house rendering broken; low = polish, omission of a small particle, ambiguity, a loose statement.

## Findings considered and refused

- 415–416, 417 σίτου: note calls it "a genitive of the thing, ‘better of food’". It agrees with the draft’s own `l` ("better … of food") and is a defensible parse (partitive with δόμεναι). Left.
- 419–421 `i` "to any man": τοίῳ ὁποῖος ἔοι is "to such a man as he might be"; "any man" is the sense of the general optatives. Left.
- 424 ἀλάπαξε has no stated object: `l` "laid waste" / `i` "brought ruin" follows new-renderings.md and the note says the object is not given. Left.
- 427–441 repeated lines: all units whose Greek equals a published unit have `l` and `i` identical to it (checked by script against odyssey-068, -004, -008, -021, and -031 for 469); the three units that only partly repeat (427, 428–430, 437–439) take the published wording line by line, and 439’s στῆναι matches the published `l`/`i` ("to stand opposed" / "to stand against them"). Left.
- 434 (τάχα δ’ ἐς πόλιν ἵκετ’ ἀϋτή) is a published unit of odyssey-068 and agrees word for word. Left.
- 447 `l` "Stand just so" vs `i` "Stand right there": both reach οὕτως; no change.
- 449 ὥς exclamatory vs the accent Murray prints: the note says exactly that. Left.
- 456 "sits at another’s table" (note) for ἀλλοτρίοισι παρήμενος: interpretive but not a label or a placement claim. Left.
- 460/483 καλά "finely" in `l`, "unscathed" / "well" in `i`: per new-renderings.md. Left.
- 474 `l` "my belly": Greek has only γαστέρος after ἔμ’; "my" is the English a literal reading needs. Left.
- 484 `i` "is perhaps here": πού is "somewhere / perhaps"; the note says the god may be among them. Left; a drafter’s call, not an error.
- 485 `i` "taking on every kind of shape" for παντοῖοι τελέθοντες: a fair sense of "becoming of every kind" (as `l` says); the note shows the literal. Left.
- 481 ὑπερφιάλως "beyond measure" and the note’s "overweening" for the adjective: consistent with the table’s ὑπερφίαλος; 482’s "overweening" in `l` is forced by the published unit (odyssey-008). Left.
- 488 `l` "their words": no pronoun in the Greek, but English needs it. Left.
- 455 note "the relative clause that follows describes the man": ὅς refers to σύ, i.e. the man; true. Left.
- 500 κήρ: `l` "black death-fate" / `i` "the black spirit of death" is exactly the table’s κῆρα μέλαιναν (15.275). Left.
- Notes: no backticks and no ASCII apostrophes anywhere (scanned); every Greek-note placement claim ("unit ends at the raised dot", "first/second half of 434", "line 439 has στῆναι") was checked against the line; all cross-references (14.257–272 and halves, 7.186, 17.370, 465 = 491, 409 = 462, 484 from 474, 411–412 and 462–463 from 503–504, 447 from 453, 506 from 492) checked and true.
- Quotation marks: every speech opens on its `mark` unit (415, 446, 454, 460, 468, 478, 483, 494, 496, 499) and closes on its last unit (444, 452, 457, 461, 476, 480, 487, 494, 497, 504); 460–461 and 478–480, 494 open and close in one unit; 453, 458, 477, 482, 488, 492, 495, 498, 505–507 are narrative and carry none; the speech that begins after 507 runs into the next part, so 507 correctly carries no mark. `l` and `i` agree in every case.
- Scansion: the packet lists no flagged lines; nothing added to any note on metre.
- Remembered English in `i`: nothing found that arrives fully formed; the new phrases (the house-table formulas for 453, 495, the "unscathed", "beyond measure") are each rebuilt in new-renderings.md from the grammar.

## Outside this part (not edited)

odyssey-085, last unit (ln 407, lines 407–408), has no closing ” and its note says "Antinous’s speech runs on into the next part". It does not: 409 (ὣς ἄρ’ ἔφη) is narration after the speech, so the speech ends at 408 and that unit should close it. The runbook forbids editing another part’s files, so this is recorded here; whoever owns 085 (already published) should add ” to its `l` and `i` and correct the note. Part 086 does not depend on it (its first unit carries no quotation mark and its note now says the speech ended at 408).

## Findings considered and refused (pass 2)

- Glosser’s flagged ἔσθι’ (478): ἔσθιε elided, imperative of ἔσθω / ἐσθίω ‘eat’; the alternative ἴσθι ‘be’ would not be elided and would double καθήμενος. Entry right. Left.
- ὤριστος (416): ὁ ἄριστος by crasis, matched by ὁ κάκιστος in the line before. Entry right. Left.
- κιχείη (476): aorist optative of ἔκιχον with the athematic ending; the subject is τέλος (‘may the end overtake Antinous’), as the entry’s quote has it. Left.
- ἐΰπλείην (466): fem. acc. sg. of ἐΰπλειος, agrees with πήρην. Left.
- λώϊον (417): the entry parses it as neut. acc. sg. of λώϊος used as a noun; consistent with the note’s ‘better of food’. Left.
- οὐλομένης (474), known entry says "perf. part."; not rewritten (the novel οὐλόμεν entry says only "part.", which holds for either).
- 456 `i` "could not bring yourself" for οὔ τί μοι ἔτλης: οὔ τι ‘at all’ is not spelled out; `l` has "in no way". Left as a defensible English.
- 478–480 `i` "by a foot or a hand" for ἢ ποδὸς ἢ καὶ χειρός: καί (‘even’) not carried; `l` has it. Left.
- 484 `i` "is perhaps here" for πού: kept from pass 1 (a drafter’s call).
- 409/462, 465/491, 468, 469, 477, 482, 498: repeated English consistent with the earlier units (checked by script).
- Gloss entries read and found right as they stand: all other novel entries (αἰτίζων, βασιλείης, βλήεται, βλημένου, γαστέρος, … ἀχρημοσύνη, ἐΰθρονον, ἔοι, ἔπεχεν, ὑπέφηνε, ὦμον etc.), and the other __broaden__ additions (βάλεν, βάλοι, δαιτὸς, δόμεναι, μνηστῆρες, περὶ, στῆθ, ἀφνειὸν, ἅλα, ἔναιον, ἠέ, ἠῶ, ὁ), each checked against the line it serves. Known-form entries for the other forms of the part were read against their lines; the gaps listed above are the only ones found.
- Scansion: none flagged; nothing added.
- Note for the owner of odyssey-085 (pass 1’s finding about its last unit lacking ” and saying the speech runs on) stands; it still cannot be edited here.
